Themes

NSH Gallery

The library's own: graphite surfaces, one citrus accent, 8-point controls and 14-point cards.

NSH Gallery: graphite dark and paper light surfaces with citrus lime (`#c6ef6a`) primary fill, continuous squircle corners, ease-out timing motion, and layered surface finishes.

Style inspiration rather than a 1:1 native clone. This theme distills the colors, radii, surfaces, and motion of NSH Gallery (other platforms). NSH Gallery ↗

A theme is one TypeScript module — index.ts for its spec, the tokens, metrics, elevation, surfaces, feedback, motion and controls defineTheme() compiles — and two files that same build exports from it: theme.json for NSH's variables and DESIGN.md for the language in words. Which tokens there are, and what each surface draws, is the Theme v5 spec on GitHub; this page reads the specs themselves.

A token is a colour, length or font family under a name, a surface is a layer a component draws itself in, and an alias is a token written as another (secondary is var(--surface)): the table shows an alias as the token it points at. The swatches follow the site's light and dark switch; the surface samples follow it too, drawn with this theme's values.

The switch calls it NSH Gallery; the registry item is theme-nsh-gallery. Show it in the preview

The build-time theme is the theme item that init writes without a flag; this item is the same data, for an app built on another theme to switch back to.

Installation

TSX nshm. The module is the theme. selectTheme switches to it while the app runs. selectTheme(null) returns to the theme the app was built with.

import nshGallery from "shadcn-nsh/themes/nsh-gallery";
import { selectTheme } from "shadcn-nsh/theme";

selectTheme(nshGallery);

CLI. init --theme nsh-gallery builds the app on this theme. add theme-nsh-gallery installs themes/nsh-gallery.ts and themes/nsh-gallery/ beside the build-time theme and leaves that one as it is.

On an app that already has a theme, init --theme nsh-gallery --overwrite replaces the build-time theme. add theme-nsh-gallery does not.

Tokens

Every token the theme sets, in theme.json's order, for light and dark: the swatch draws the value and the text is what the file writes. A var(--x) or a color-mix() is the theme's own reference; the swatch fills it in from the same appearance, the text leaves it as written.

Surfaces

The surfaces this theme draws, in the schema's order: the tokens are the ones its values name, and the sample is drawn from the spec itself — the background, the gradient, the shadow and the edges it writes, with its references filled in and the shadow taken from the theme's own elevation scale.

SurfaceWhat it drawsRead byTokensSample
cardA section's ground: the theme's base surface, with its hairline and contact shadow.Card, Panel, Tablecard, foreground, border
raisedA tile standing on a card: the lifted face with a lit top edge and a soft shadow.Button (raised), Segmented, a tab's thumbsurface, foreground, border
insetA well cut into a card: the recessed ground inputs and code sit in, shadow turned in.Input, Textarea, a code blockforeground, border
channelA narrow recess one step softer than a well: the groove a track or a divider sits in.A slider's rail, a progress trackforeground, border
plateA slim raised strip: the bar a toolbar or a row of tabs rests on.Toolbar, Tabs' listforeground, card, border, surface
overlayA floating panel above the page: the popover ground with the largest lift.Popover, DropdownMenu, Selectpopover, foreground, border
modalThe heaviest floating ground: a dialog, a sheet, an alert.Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheetcard, foreground, border
inverseThe flipped ground: dark on a light page, for a strip that has to stand apart.Toast, a caption over mediacard, foreground, border
glassA translucent pane over content: blurred, tinted, lit along its top edge.A title bar, a floating toolbarforeground, border, popover, card
accentThe accent fill and the ink that sits on it.A primary Button, Badge (accent)primary, primary-foreground
fillThe accent in its lit form: a gradient, a firm edge and a shadow under it.A primary Button, a switch's thumb (on)primary-foreground
